newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev weakens against mark, rises vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev weakens against mark, rises vs dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 999-1,000 per mark on Thursday, weaker than 998-1,000 at the opening and 997-1,000 at Wednesday's close, as foreign currency demand from banks and clients outweighed supply.

* Local banks were seen buying foreign currency to profit from higher interest rates on deposits while investors were converting lev proceeds from treasury paper sales into foreign currency for the same reason.

* Overnight interbank lev deposit rates have stood at 1.50-1.75 annual this week, under the central bank main interest rate of 5.42 percent, against three percent on mark deposits and around five percent on dollar deposits.
* Traders said the lev could not weaken beyond 1,000 per mark, the fixed ask price of the central bank under the currency board system.
* The lev rose to 1,829-1,832 to the dollar from 1,830-1,835 in the morning and 1,839-1,842 at Wednesday's close, tracking the mark/dollar rise on international markets.
* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 to the mark as an anchor under an IMF-prescribed currency board system, a fixed exchange rate mechanism introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the currency.
* Under the system Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at a fixed bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
